METHODS OF TEST FOR PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS: DETERMINATION OF TRACE ELEMENTS IN PETROLEUM PRODUCTS : TOTAL CHLORINE (WICKBOLD OXY-HYDROGEN COMBUSTION METHOD) [P : 81,]
(First Reprint MARCH1983) UDC 665.6/.7:543.064:546.13
Adapted from IP 243/7OT Sulphw in Petroleum Products Wickbold Oxy-hydrogen Method and IP .N4/69T Chlorine in Petroleum Producls Flask CombustionMethod 1. SCOPE 1.1 This methodSscribes a rapid procedure for the determination of trace It is applicable to chlorine contents amounts of chlorine in organic liquids. ranging from 0 to. 500 ppm and is suitable for liquids in the volatility range up to and including gas oils.
rhT?2 - The method should not be used indkcriminately (for example, sulphur, bromine) may intiue. a~ other trace materials

2. OUTLINE

OF THE

MFZHOD

2.1 Depending on the chlorine content 5 to 100 g of sample is rapidly burnt in an oxy-hydrogen flame. The hydrochloric acid formed is absorbed in distilled water, converted to sodium chloride by addition ofsodium hydroxide and titrated with standard mercuric nitrate solution, using diphenyl carbazone as indicator. 3. 6.4 Pass primary oxygen through the apparatus at a rate of 16 litres per minute and secondary oxygen at a rate of approximately 3 litres per minute at the same time opening the vacuum control value E until flow through the flow indicator stops. Then close stopcock & and adjust the vacuum control valve E to obtain a pressure of 26.7k6.7 mbar (20&5 mmHg) below atmospheric in the three-necked flask as indicated by the manometer. 6.5 Remove the spray trap from the absorption column and hold in one hand; with the other hand pour 50 ml of water into the absorber column, Replace the spray trap. 6.6 Take out the burner. Open the hydrogen valve A .until a hydrogen Allow the hydrogen ta pass for flow rate of O-8 litre per minute is achieved. 30 seconds. Now ignite the hydrogen with a tint or battery-operated 6

Place the burner in the combuslighter or wax taper (do not use matches). tion tube taking care that the flame does not touch the wa!i of the standard joint. The pressure as measured by the manometer will now drop. Restore the pressure to approximately 26.7 mbar (20 mmHg) below atmospheric by manipulating the vacuum control valve E. CAUTION ! Keep the burner mouth well away from the condenser opening during the 30 second flushing with hydrogen so as to prevent an explosive mixture of oxygen and hydrogen from entering the condenser. 6.7 Bring the sample in position, taking care that the sample inlet of the burner nearly reaches the bottom of the bottle. 6.8 Start the combustion by partially opening the burner stopcock P. -4djust the flame length using the burner stopcock P until the flame is approximately three-quarters of the length of combustion tube (see CAUTION). Start the stopcock. If the burner stopcock P is fully open further adjustment may be made using the vacuum control valve E. CAUTION ! Should the burner flame extinguish at any time, first turn off the hydrogen at valve A turn off the sample supply at source, remove the burner and then quickly turn off the oxygen at valve G. Abandon the determination and prepare the apparatus for another determination as described in 5. XOX 1 - lf a sample shows poor combustion, read the pressure on the manometer.
Improve combustion by increasing the secondary oxygen flow rate and sure on the manometer by manipulating the vacuum control valve E. SOTE 2 -The occurrence of vapour bubbles between stopcock P indicates that too much suction is applied for the particular type of cases reduce the suction (valve Ej and open stopcock P wider to restore restore the presand the burner sample. In such sample feed rate.

6.9 When the sample has been burnt, wash the sample bottle with three successive 2 ml portions of iso-octane or diluent solvent as appropriate. .Wow earh portion to burn, keeping the sample inlet filled all the time. Remove the sample bottle and gradually open the burner stopcock until the burner is emptied by suction taking care to maintain a slight vacuum in the three-nrckrd flask. Close the burner stopcock P. 6.10 Kestore the pressure in the three-necked flask to approximately 26.7 mbar (20 mmHg) below atmospheric and close the hydrogen valve A. Stop Allow the burner to remain in place until the flame is extinguished. the stopcock. Take the burner out of the combustion tube, close the oxygen valves I and 3 and the vacuum control valve E. Open the flow control indicator stopcock &. Switch off the vacuum pump. Lift the spray trap and allow the absorber solution to drain into the receiving flask. Remove the adaptor from the central neck of the flask. 6.11 Rinse the condenser, the splash bulb and the absorber abundantly \vith water, collecting the washings in the three-necked flask. Transfer the liquid quantitatively to a 500-d conical flask and add 1 drop of phenolphthalein indicator solution. Make the solution slightly alkaline by Evaporate the dropwisc addition of 2 perctnt sodium hydroxide solution. 7

soIutiun to a volume of apProximatety 50 ml and transfer it. to a IOO-ml volumetric flask. Wash the conical &sk with water and transfer the washings to make the volume of solution to 100 ml. 6.12 Pipette 50 ml of of bromophenol blue Neutralize the solution 0.5 ml excess (see Note the solution into a conical flask. Add 2 or 3 drops and 1 ml of barium nitrate solution (see Note 1). with 0.1 N nitric acid to a yellow colour and add 2).

NOTE l- Barium nitrate solution k added to precipitate any sulphw present as barium sulphate, because sulphur interferes with the titration. The addition of 1 ml of barium nitmte may be omitted if no sukphur is present or may be increased, if found insufficient. NOTE 2 - The prescribed acidification provids a satisfactory PH range of 3.0 to 3.5.

6.13 Add 0.5 ml (app roximately 10 drops) of diphenyl carbazone indicator and titrate slowly with standard mercuric nitrate solution using a microburette, until a definite pink end point is obtained. Record the volume to nearest 0.01 nil.
